text: You used to have a dog like this…
Ha-ha!  An amusing cat photo.
Excellent pictures of nature.
Food photos… your stomach rumbles!
Some very interesting travel photos.
Pictures of a concert of popular band.
Photos of someone's luxurious house.
A folder full of colorful cartoon ponies.  Someone spent hours drawing all these little horses.
Photos of a furry convention.  The elaborate costumes must have been hot to wear.
Anime screenshots and fan art, carefully sorted into folders.  You wonder how the series ended.
You feel nostalgic as you stare at the photo.
A row of people squint into the sun while someone just out of frame tells them to move closer together.
A blurry phone photograph shows a rainbow over an entirely ordinary parking lot.
Someone has taken a close-up photograph of a particularly satisfying snow angel.
The camera went off inside a pocket.  The next picture is a remarkably detailed view of a confused nose.
A child beams beside a birthday cake.  Each candle seems impossibly bright.
Someone tried to take a serious family portrait.  In every shot, a different person is laughing.
A picnic blanket, paper plates, and a whole afternoon with nothing urgent to do.
Blurry holiday photos show three generations crowded around the same small table.
A dog proudly carries a stick far too large to fit through the door.
The same cat occupies a succession of increasingly unsuitable cardboard boxes.
Someone photographed a sleeping hamster from what must have been every possible angle.
A muddy paw print on a clean couch is followed by a portrait of a dog doing its best to look innocent.
A crooked roadside photograph captures a mountain disappearing into clouds.  It must have been worth the drive.
Beach umbrellas dot a stretch of brilliant blue water.  Nobody in the picture appears to be in a hurry.
Someone has photographed every meal, hotel room, and slightly different view from the same balcony.
An airport window frames the wing of a plane at sunset.  Once, going far away was this simple.
A fox peers out from tall grass, apparently just as surprised as the photographer.
A long exposure turns a waterfall into a white ribbon between mossy rocks.
Most of the bird photographs contain branches, empty sky, or a tiny departing blur.  One is perfect.
Stars wheel over a dark campsite.  For a moment, the photograph makes the world feel quiet.
A tray of golden pastries is followed by an almost identical tray with one suspiciously empty space.
An elaborate restaurant dessert occupies the center of a very large, otherwise empty plate.
A sequence of bread-making photos ends with a dense little loaf and a handwritten note: "Still edible!"
Someone carefully arranged a homemade dinner for the camera.  Their thumb covers half the lens.
A miniature railway winds through a painstakingly built landscape.  Even the tiny station has flower boxes.
Half-painted tabletop figures surround a mug labeled "definitely not paint water".
A costume takes shape across dozens of progress photographs, ending with an exhausted but triumphant mirror selfie.
A shelf slowly fills with handmade pottery.  The earliest lopsided cups have been given the most prominent places.
Wasted time, these pictures do not provoke your senses.
